suggestions.reason: The baseline produces a genuinely strong, constraint-adapted HIPAA/AWS architecture — arguably richer compliance mapping (Section 7 Security Rule citations) than the skill run. The discriminating value of the eval comes almost entirely from the prescribed-structure assertions (exact section names: Constraints & Assumptions, Tech Stack, Capability → Tech Mapping, Key Architecture Decisions, Research Suggestions, Depth marker) plus the librarian/researcher delegation assertions. These correctly separate skill (14/14) from baseline (6/14).

Section-name assertions are strict-heading matches. The baseline covers the same content under different headings, so it fails purely on naming. This is intended (the skill enforces a consistent template), but if the goal were to test substance rather than template adherence these would be false negatives. Worth being explicit in the assertion that the exact heading from OUTPUT_FORMAT is required.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions discriminate cleanly. Constraint-adaptation assertions fairly pass for both runs (the constraints are in the prompt); the structure, capability-mapping, ADR, research-suggestions, depth, researcher-delegation, and librarian assertions are what the skill uniquely satisfies.
